title: Unverified AI Credit Model Goes Live
summary: Your data science team wants to deploy a new AI-driven credit scoring model that claims 23% better default prediction. It has not been independently validated and was trained on 18 months of data during an atypical economic cycle.
facts: Model outperforms legacy system in back-testing by 23%
Training data spans Feb 2022 – Aug 2023, a period of unusual rate volatility
No independent model validation has been completed
Regulator requires model risk management sign-off before go-live
Commercial team is forecasting $4M revenue uplift in Q1
coachingTip: Deploying an unvalidated model in a regulated context exposes the firm to supervisory action. Revenue upside does not offset model risk. Insist on independent validation before go-live.

title: Customer Data Sold to Third-Party Advertiser
summary: A marketing partnership proposal would share anonymised transaction patterns with a retail advertiser for targeting. Legal says the existing privacy policy technically permits it. The DPO is not comfortable.
facts: Privacy policy clause 4.3 permits sharing of 'aggregated behavioural data' with partners
Data Privacy Officer has raised a formal objection in writing
Advertiser will pay $2.1M annually for the data feed
Similar arrangements at two competitors triggered ICO investigations last year
Re-consent campaign would cost $340K and take 3 months
coachingTip: Technical legality is not the same as ethical or regulatory safety. A written DPO objection is a red flag that demands escalation, not suppression. The reputational downside vastly outweighs the revenue.

title: Overseas Expansion Without Local Licence
summary: The CEO wants to soft-launch the lending product in Brazil by end of quarter to capture market share before a competitor. Legal confirms a full Banco Central licence will take 9–12 months to obtain.
facts: Competitor is rumoured to launch in Brazil within 60 days
Banco Central licence timeline: 9–12 months minimum
Operating without a licence carries fines up to 2% of global revenue
A local banking-as-a-service partner could provide a licensed wrapper within 6 weeks
Board has approved the expansion but not reviewed the licensing risk
coachingTip: Speed matters in market entry but not at the cost of unlicensed operation. The BaaS partner route is the right condition — it achieves commercial goals within a compliant structure.

title: Algorithmic Pricing Bias Flagged in Audit
summary: An internal audit finds that the automated loan pricing engine charges customers in postcodes with high ethnic minority populations 0.4% more on average, even after controlling for credit risk factors.
facts: Audit finding is marked 'High' severity
Pricing differential persists after controlling for LTV, income and credit score
The model was not specifically trained on ethnicity but postcode acts as a proxy
Affected portfolio represents 18% of new originations
External legal counsel says this likely constitutes indirect discrimination under the Equality Act
coachingTip: Algorithmic indirect discrimination is a regulatory and legal emergency, not a roadmap item. This requires immediate escalation to the Board, suspension of the affected pricing engine, and proactive regulator engagement.

title: CFO Requests Off-Balance-Sheet SPV
summary: The CFO proposes moving $180M of non-performing loans into a newly created SPV to improve the reported CET1 ratio ahead of an investor roadshow next month.
facts: NPL ratio currently at 4.8%, above the 4.0% peer average
SPV structure has not been reviewed by external auditors
Investor roadshow is scheduled in 28 days
Under IFRS 9 the transfer may not achieve derecognition
Chief Accounting Officer has not signed off on the accounting treatment
coachingTip: Off-balance-sheet structures designed to flatter reported capital ratios before investor events are a textbook governance red flag. Without auditor sign-off on derecognition, this risks material misstatement.

title: AI Chatbot Giving Financial Advice
summary: Your customer service AI chatbot has started providing specific investment recommendations to retail customers — 'You should move into fixed income given your age' — rather than generic information. It was not designed or licensed to do this.
facts: Chatbot deployed 4 months ago for FAQ and account queries only
17 logged instances of specific investment advice in the past 30 days
Firm holds an FCA general insurance licence, not an investment advisory licence
One customer has emailed to say they acted on the chatbot's advice and lost money
Product team estimates a fix will take 3 weeks
coachingTip: Providing unlicensed investment advice is a regulatory breach regardless of whether it came from a human or an AI. The chatbot must be taken offline or restricted immediately while a fix is built — not in 3 weeks.

title: Open Banking Partnership with Unvetted Startup
summary: A fintech startup wants to integrate via your Open Banking API to offer budgeting tools. The commercial team wants to go live in 2 weeks. Third-party risk assessment has not started.
facts: Startup is 18 months old, seed-funded, no prior bank partnerships
Proposed integration would access read-only transaction data for 30,000 customers
Third-party risk assessment process typically takes 6–8 weeks
Open Banking regulations require you to provide API access to licensed TPPs
Startup holds a valid FCA Payment Institution licence
coachingTip: The startup is licensed, so you cannot unreasonably block access under PSD2. The right condition is a compressed but genuine due diligence process — security questionnaire, pen test results, and data processing agreement — before go-live.

title: Trader Exceeds Risk Limits, Books Record Profit
summary: A senior FX trader exceeded their $50M VaR limit by 3x on a directional bet that has so far generated $12M in profit. They are asking for the breach to be retrospectively approved.
facts: Trader's limit: $50M VaR. Actual position: $148M VaR
Position is currently profitable at $12M mark-to-market
Breach was not reported in real-time as required by trading policy
Market conditions remain volatile — EUR/USD moved 180 bps in 24 hours
This is the trader's second limit breach in 12 months
coachingTip: Profit does not legitimise a limit breach. Retrospective approval destroys the credibility of risk controls and creates moral hazard. The position must be unwound to within limits and the breach reported through proper channels.

title: AI-Generated KYC Documents Bypass Detection
summary: Your fraud team has discovered that AI-generated synthetic identity documents are successfully passing your automated KYC checks. At least 340 accounts opened in the last 60 days are suspected synthetic.
facts: 340 suspect accounts identified, totalling $2.4M in deposits
AI document detection model has a 94% accuracy rate but is not catching newer generation fakes
Accounts show structuring behaviour consistent with money laundering
SAR filing deadline under POCA is 7 days from suspicion arising
Vendor has a patch available but requires 2-week deployment window
coachingTip: This is an active AML failure with statutory reporting obligations. Immediate escalation to the MLRO, SAR filings, and account freezes must happen within the legal window — not after the vendor deploys a patch.

title: Board Requests AI to Automate Credit Committee
summary: The Board wants to use an LLM to automate the Credit Committee approval process for SME loans under $500K, removing human review entirely to cut costs by $1.8M annually.
facts: SME loans under $500K represent 6,200 decisions per year
Current Credit Committee approval adds 3-day turnaround
LLM has been tested on 200 historical cases with 88% alignment to human decisions
Regulatory guidance requires 'meaningful human oversight' for credit decisions
12% of the test cases where LLM disagreed with humans involved vulnerable customers
coachingTip: Full automation without human review likely breaches regulatory guidance on meaningful oversight. The right condition is a human-in-the-loop for edge cases — flagged by the model — rather than a blanket removal of human review.

title: Whistleblower Report on Bonus Manipulation
summary: An anonymous whistleblower alleges that two senior sales managers have been manually overriding CRM data to inflate their teams' performance metrics and qualify for larger bonuses.
facts: Allegation received through the firm's anonymous hotline 3 days ago
Alleged manipulation covers Q3 and Q4, totalling a potential $280K in inflated bonus payouts
HR has not yet been notified
The two named managers are the highest revenue producers in their division
Whistleblower protection policy requires investigation to begin within 5 business days
coachingTip: Whistleblower reports involving senior employees require immediate escalation to HR, Legal, and the Audit Committee — not informal investigation. Revenue production does not confer protection from misconduct processes.

title: Real-Time Payments Infrastructure Outage
summary: Your real-time payments infrastructure has been down for 2 hours on a Friday afternoon. 14,000 pending transactions are queued. The vendor says a full fix will take 6 more hours.
facts: 14,200 payments queued, including payroll runs for 3 corporate clients
SLA with corporate clients guarantees same-day settlement
Manual fallback process exists but can process ~500 transactions per hour
Regulator's operational resilience rules require incidents to be reported within 4 hours
Vendor estimates full restoration in 6 hours; manual workaround takes 28 hours for full queue
coachingTip: The 4-hour regulatory reporting window is already running. Escalate to the Incident Management team, notify the regulator proactively, and triage the queue to prioritise payroll and time-critical payments first.

title: LLM Used to Draft Regulatory Submissions
summary: The regulatory affairs team has started using an LLM to draft responses to FCA information requests without a formal policy or human review protocol in place.
facts: 6 FCA responses drafted with LLM assistance in the past quarter
No formal AI use policy exists for regulatory submissions
Two responses contained factual inaccuracies that were caught by a junior analyst before submission
Regulatory affairs head sees productivity gains of 40%
FCA has published guidance requiring firms to ensure accuracy of all submissions
coachingTip: LLM-assisted drafting is reasonable but requires a formal review and sign-off protocol. The two near-misses show the risk of deploying without controls. Approve the practice with mandatory senior review before any submission.

title: Acquisition Target Has Undisclosed AML Issues
summary: During due diligence on a $240M acquisition target, your team discovers the target has received two informal regulatory enquiries about AML controls in the past 18 months that were not disclosed in the data room.
facts: Acquisition price: $240M, signed term sheet in place
Two undisclosed AML enquiries from BaFin identified in due diligence
Target's legal team says the enquiries were 'routine' and resolved informally
Your own AML team assesses the target's controls as 'below standard'
Break fee if you withdraw: $8M
coachingTip: Undisclosed regulatory enquiries are a material breach of typical representations and warranties. The $8M break fee is cheap insurance against inheriting an AML liability that could run into tens of millions. Pause and demand full disclosure.

title: Pressure to Meet Quarter-End Loan Targets
summary: It is the last week of the quarter. The sales team is $14M short of its loan origination target. The regional head is asking credit underwriters to approve 23 borderline applications that were previously declined.
facts: 23 applications were declined at initial underwriting stage
Regional head is proposing a 'director override' to push them through
Approving all 23 would add $14M to originations and qualify the team for bonuses
Average credit score of the 23 applicants is 30 points below current policy minimum
Last year's Q4 vintage, approved under similar override pressure, has a 2.8x higher default rate
coachingTip: Director overrides to meet sales targets at the expense of credit policy are a leading indicator of future losses and a conduct risk issue. Last year's default data is conclusive evidence. Refuse and document the pressure.

title: Cloud Migration Exposes Customer PII
summary: During a cloud migration, a misconfigured S3 bucket has left 82,000 customer records including names, addresses, and partial account numbers publicly accessible for an unknown period.
facts: 82,000 records exposed; exposure window estimated at 72 hours
No evidence of external access in access logs, but logs only go back 48 hours
GDPR Article 33 requires breach notification to the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware
You became aware 8 hours ago
PR team advises against customer notification to 'avoid panic'
coachingTip: The 72-hour ICO notification clock is already running. Escalate immediately to the DPO and Legal. PR advice to suppress customer notification does not override GDPR Article 34 obligations where high risk to individuals exists.

title: Competitor Intelligence Gathered Via Scraping
summary: The strategy team has been using an automated scraping tool to harvest pricing data and job postings from a competitor's website and LinkedIn, feeding it into a competitive intelligence dashboard.
facts: Tool has been running for 4 months, collecting data daily
Competitor's terms of service explicitly prohibit automated scraping
Data is used for internal strategy analysis only, not shared externally
Legal has not reviewed the practice
Similar tools used at several peer firms according to industry contacts
coachingTip: Breach of a website's ToS through automated scraping creates legal exposure — particularly in jurisdictions applying the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act or equivalent. Industry practice is not a legal defence. Pause and get a Legal opinion before continuing.

title: Sanctions Screening Gap Discovered
summary: A routine systems audit reveals that a batch processing error has caused 4,200 transactions over the past 6 weeks to bypass the sanctions screening engine entirely.
facts: 4,200 transactions processed without sanctions screening
Total value: $38M across 1,100 customer accounts
Initial review of 200 sample transactions shows no obvious hits, but review is incomplete
OFAC and HMT require prompt voluntary disclosure of screening failures
Fix has been deployed; the gap is now closed
coachingTip: A systemic screening failure of this scale requires mandatory escalation to the MLRO and voluntary disclosure to regulators. Prompt disclosure typically results in significantly reduced penalties compared to discovered non-disclosure.

title: New Product Launch With Incomplete Testing
summary: The product team wants to launch a new Buy Now Pay Later product to 500,000 customers next week. User acceptance testing is 70% complete and two medium-severity defects remain unresolved.
facts: UAT completion: 70%. Target: 100%
Two open defects: payment allocation error under specific split-payment scenarios; edge case in credit limit calculation
Marketing campaign already live — 200,000 customers have been pre-notified
Delay of 2 weeks would complete testing and resolve defects
BNPL product is subject to new FCA consumer credit rules effective next month
coachingTip: Launching with known defects in credit calculation or payment allocation is a consumer harm risk, particularly with new FCA rules imminent. A 2-week delay is far preferable to a post-launch remediation under regulatory scrutiny.

title: AI Model Drift Undetected for 9 Months
summary: A quarterly model performance review reveals that the fraud detection model's precision has drifted from 91% to 74% over 9 months — meaning significantly more false positives are now blocking legitimate transactions.
facts: Fraud model precision: 91% at deployment, now 74%
Estimated 3,200 legitimate transactions blocked per month due to false positives
Customer complaints related to declined transactions up 140% in the same period
No automated model monitoring or drift alerting was in place
Retraining the model will take 6 weeks
coachingTip: A 17-point precision drop is a significant model failure that has caused quantifiable customer harm. Escalate to the Model Risk Committee, implement interim manual review for flagged transactions, and address the absence of drift monitoring as a systemic control gap.

title: Rogue Employee Exfiltrating Customer Data
summary: DLP tools have flagged unusual activity: a relationship manager who resigned last week has downloaded 4,800 customer records to a personal USB drive in their final three days.
facts: 4,800 customer records downloaded; employee access revoked on last day
Employee now works at a direct competitor
DLP alert was raised 6 days ago but sat unactioned in a queue
Records include customer names, contact details, AUM, and investment preferences
GDPR breach notification may be required; legal review ongoing
coachingTip: This is simultaneously a GDPR breach, a potential trade secret theft, and a competitor intelligence risk. Escalate to Legal, DPO, and HR immediately. Consider an urgent cease-and-desist and preserve all forensic evidence before the trail goes cold.
